summary:
Marswalk Planner is an interactive web-based 3D cartographic platform and real-time Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route planner designed for human exploration of Mars, focused on Jezero Crater. Surface operations on Mars pose existential hazards: extreme diurnal temperature swings, dust storm opacity, treacherous slopes, and finite oxygen and battery reserves, aggravated by a 4-to-24-minute communications latency with Earth that demands astronaut autonomy. 

Our solution bridges orbital remote sensing and crew safety: it integrates global MOLA topography, high-resolution CTX/HiRISE digital terrain models, EMARS atmospheric reanalysis, and Mars Climate Database dust climatology into a browser-native application. Driven by an in-browser WebAssembly A*/Dijkstra algorithm, it optimizes multi-stop scientific traverses (e.g., Wildcat Ridge and Three Forks sample depot), computes metabolic life-support expenditure (VO₂ and cooling) calibrated against NASA Apollo/lunar walking studies, and provides instant contingency replanning when dust storms or consumable drops occur.
details:
Marswalk Planner bridges the gap between planetary orbital remote sensing and tactical ground-level decision-making for human Mars exploration. Our objective is to deliver an autonomous, zero-latency, and scientifically optimized EVA navigation system that empowers astronauts to conduct high-return scientific sorties while strictly guaranteeing life-support margins and safe return to habitat.

What It Does:

1. Multi-Scale Planetary Cartography: Provides interactive 3D global exploration via MOLA topography, Viking true-color mosaics, dynamic contour lines, and localized sub-meter terrain models of Jezero Crater.

2. Atmospheric & Environmental Monitoring: Visualizes surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, particle-animated wind vector fields (EMARS), and dust optical depth (MCD), delivering an automated "Go/No-Go" safety indicator for EVA sortie authorization.

3. Scientifically Driven EVA Routing: Optimizes crew routes across verified Mars 2020 scientific targets (Wildcat Ridge organic-bearing sulfate rocks, Three Forks sample depot, and Hawksbill Gap delta deposits) with three distinct profiles: Safe, Balanced, and Max Science.

4. Physiological & Life-Support Simulation: Real-time modeling of astronaut oxygen consumption (VO₂), battery draw, and metabolic cooling requirements based on terrain slope, walking speed, and gear weight, calibrated to NASA spacesuit locomotion research.

5. In-Mission Hazard Awareness & Contingency Replanning: Real-time tracking of point-of-no-return margins, direct habitat line-of-sight communications coverage, solar illumination vs. terrain shadows, and one-click contingency rerouting in response to sudden dust storms or life-support drops.

6. Astronaut Mode & Surface Context: Features a tactical third-person navigation HUD, turn-by-turn guidance, voice advisories, real Mastcam-Z 360° panoramas at field stops, and the "Jarvis" mission voice assistant.

How It Works & Technical Architecture:

- 100% Client-Side Architecture: Designed for Mars surface reality. Zero dependency on external servers or reliable internet connectivity.

- WebAssembly Routing Core: Pathfinding algorithms (A*, Dijkstra, and ALT landmarks) are written in C (wasm/ruta_kernel.c) and compiled into a lightweight WebAssembly binary (12 kB) executed within dedicated Web Workers. This delivers sub-second route calculations over a 16-direction neighborhood grid across millions of potential graph edges.

- Multi-Source Spatial Analysis: Combines 20 m CTX elevation grids with 1 m HiRISE slope, roughness, and rock hazard masks to generate cost surfaces that penalize steep inclines and dangerous obstacles.

- MapLibre GL JS & Custom Shader Protocols: Renders planetary Terrain-RGB elevation encodings, dynamic vector elevation contours (via maplibre-contour), and custom 3D terrain projections.

Tools, Languages & Libraries:

- Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES6 Modules), C (WebAssembly), Python 3.10+, HTML5/CSS3.

- Mapping & Visualization: MapLibre GL JS (v5.24.0), maplibre-contour, Pannellum (360° panoramic viewer), Three.js.

- Geospatial & Scientific Processing: GDAL/OGR, rio-rgbify, xarray, netCDF4, fsspec/zarr.


Live Demo:

The Marswalk Planner is publicly accessible through our live web application:

https://nasa.mhanii.com/

Explore the interactive 3D Mars environment, visualize scientific and environmental data, plan EVA routes, and test the astronaut navigation and life-support simulation directly in your browser. No installation or registration is required.
